sources.title: Serre's modularity conjecture (I)
sources.edition: Author's preprint (results.pdf) of the paper published as Invent. Math. 178 (2009), 485–504. Locators give the preprint's page numbers
readSections: §1, p. 2 (S-type, residual modularity and residual weight conventions); §1.5, p. 4 (Galois, local-group and character notation); §4, pp. 6–7, especially Theorem 4.1 and the preceding lift/weight conventions.

reusedNodes.use: Bind the residual-modularity witness adapter owned by R22.5; preserve α only in dyadic residual weight 2 and β in both dyadic residual weights.
Bind the full R22.5 odd-prime and R22.6 dyadic exports to a supplied lift, preserving every case guard. This is not an independent lifting proof.

importChecks.statement: For a modular S-type residual representation over ℚ, normalized to 2≤k(ρ̄)≤p+1 at odd p, the weight/level adapter supplies α and β over an allowable soluble totally real field unramified at p that preserves the residual image conditions. For p=2 it supplies β in residual weights 2 and 4, and α only in residual weight 2. α is witnessed by a cuspidal form of parallel weight k(ρ̄), unramified above p; β by a cuspidal form of parallel weight 2 and local conductor exponent at most one above p. The witnesses may differ.

sources.match: The two residual witness conditions and the passage from modularity over ℚ to those conditions; the dyadic α qualification and the harmless enlargement of prime-to-p level are explicit.

acceptance: An unramified weight-two witness with k(ρ̄)=2 witnesses both predicates.
A weight-two Steinberg witness has local conductor exponent one and witnesses β, but that witness is not an α-witness.
A weight-two witness of conductor exponent two does not witness β; the existence of another witness is a separate question.
Dyadic residual weight 4 gives β, with no asserted α-witness.

A Katz eigenform alone is not the required characteristic-zero witness. The adapter must supply a residual eigenvector in the appropriate integral cusp-lattice reduction at the required weight, level and character, or an independently justified characteristic-zero witness. A Hasse-power weight shift does not establish the prescribed α/β weight.
The R20.6 case table is a manifest, not a small-prime proof export. Its rows invoking later R27 Serre modularity cannot close an input to Theorem 4.1 without a separate acyclic argument.
importChecks.proofBoundary: The R15.2 reduction-image construction and R15.5 lifting theorem were read in their accepted owner packet. Same-weight lifting is conditional on an actual integral reduction eigenvector; holomorphic fine-level base change is not an unrestricted cusp/character theorem. Their invertible-level hypotheses do not automatically cover the β level Np. These are obligations of the R22.5 residual adapter, not added assumptions on the source Theorem 4.1.

importChecks.statement: Let ρ̄:G_ℚ→GL₂(𝔽) be continuous and modular, with 𝔽 finite of characteristic p, and let ρ:G_ℚ→GL₂(𝒪) be a continuous lift, with 𝒪 the integers of a finite extension of ℚ_p and reduction isomorphic to ρ̄. Assume finite ramification. At p=2 require nonsolvable residual image and det ρ(c)=−1, and assume crystalline weight 2 or semistable weight 2 with k(ρ̄)=4 in the latter branch. At p>2 require absolute irreducibility of ρ̄ restricted to G_{ℚ(μ_p)}, normalized residual weight 2≤k(ρ̄)≤p+1, and assume crystalline weight k with 2≤k≤p+1 or potentially semistable weight 2. Weight k uses Hodge–Tate weights {0,k−1}. Then ρ is modular, meaning it is isomorphic after coefficient extension to the representation of a characteristic-zero cuspidal eigenform. The lift is an input, not an existence conclusion.

sources.match: The full modularity conclusion, coefficient/lift and weight conventions, and separate dyadic and odd-prime hypotheses.

sources.locator: §10.2 and Remark, p. 92; Theorem 9.7 and proof, pp. 89–90
sources.match: Theorem 9.7 and cited lifting cases prove the theorem without global finiteness or potential modularity. Its self-contained range does not include the full crystalline endpoint with residual weight 2.

acceptance: A modular residual representation of nonsolvable image in characteristic 2 with an odd crystalline weight-two lift is covered.
The dyadic semistable branch with residual weight 2 cannot be used; the crystalline branch remains a separate sufficient condition.
An even dyadic lift cannot be accepted from its reduction: the determinant signs coincide modulo 2.
At odd p, crystalline weight p+2 is outside the claimed crystalline interval.
The nonordinary crystalline endpoint k=p+1 with k(ρ̄)=2 requires the full R22.5 export, including its Kisin proof leaf.
General odd-prime potentially semistable weight two cannot be replaced by the narrower Theorem 9.7 local-type statement.
No step asks for R24.1 finiteness, R24.2 arithmetic points or R24.3 lift existence.

Do not substitute the narrower Theorem 9.7 statement.

Realise the existing Theorem 4.1(1) arithmetic signature with a supplied continuous lift, nonsolvable image, characteristic-zero oddness and the distinct crystalline/semistable weight-two guards. Keep the residual nonfinite/weight-four comparison in its owner.

Close the small-prime portions of the existing R22.5 residual adapter: p=2 prime-to-2 level at residual weight 2, weight-two level of 2-adic exponent at most one at residual weights 2 and 4, and p=3/enlarged-level guards. Supply characteristic-zero cuspidal witnesses. R20.6/strong-form-case-table is a manifest: its R27 rows do not constitute proof exports and cannot be used here if they depend on Theorem 4.1. Supply the weaker, nonoptimal-level witness result needed by KW II §10.2 p.92 through a lower-tier, acyclic proof.

Justify the passage to characteristic-zero cuspidal witnesses of precisely weight k(ρ̄), prime-to-p level for α, and weight 2, level dividing Np for β, including the character and specified Hecke operators. If using the accepted R15.2/R15.5 interfaces, supply an actual integral reduction eigenvector or the cusp/character base-change criterion at the required weight and level; their invertible-level theorem is not by itself the β level-Np bridge. Alternatively supply a direct classical witness argument. Arbitrary Hasse weight shifts or a Katz eigenform alone do not discharge this request.

gaps.title: Inherited nonordinary crystalline endpoint
gaps.detail: R22.5 explicitly leaves unread Kisin, Modularity of some geometric Galois representations, Durham proceedings [38] in KW II. The source assertion is read in §10.2 p.92, but the endpoint proof k=p+1 and k(ρ̄)=2 is not closed by this consumer pass.

gaps.title: Small-prime residual witness suppliers
gaps.detail: R20.3/R20.4 retain p=2/p=3 restrictions. R20.6/strong-form-case-table is a manifest, with some rows naming R27 Serre modularity rather than providing a lower-tier proof. Those rows cannot silently close the residual adapter feeding Theorem 4.1. The open request needs the weaker witness result of KW II §10.2 p.92 with an acyclic proof; no optimal-level theorem is required.

gaps.title: Same-weight characteristic-zero residual witnesses
gaps.detail: The accepted R15.2/integral-lattice-and-reduction-image and R15.5/reduction-to-weight-at-least-two-and-to-a-true-eigenform supply only conditional lifting from an actual integral reduction eigenvector. Fine-level holomorphic base change does not automatically prove the required cusp/character result, and their invertible-level hypotheses do not directly cover β at level Np. A weight-shifted Katz form need not have α weight k(ρ̄) or β weight 2. The R22.5 adapter must establish the exact classical witnesses (or the appropriate reduction-image criterion), at every prime where it uses this bridge. This is a supplier proof gap, not a claimed error in KW Theorem 4.1.

gaps.title: Arithmetic signatures and remaining lifting branch checks
gaps.detail: The baseline supplies algebraic representations and G_ℚ, not the full residual lattice/newform Galois comparison, local Hodge predicates and Serre-weight interfaces needed by these consumer signatures. The ordinary endpoint hypotheses and the unprinted finite-inertia twist reduction stay with the R22.5 supplier. The suggested file lists both full signatures as omissions and checks only concrete determinant matrices.
